observation.visible_scene: A diagonal column of pale, translucent liquid enters from the upper-left edge of the frame and arcs downward to the right, striking a dark, wet paved surface near the lower-right corner. At the impact point a bright white splash and a fan of scattered airborne droplets are visible. The background is out of focus, showing a strip of green grass above a low curb. The overall geometry of the stream and its landing point stay in the same screen positions throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The stream's entry point (top-left) and impact point (bottom-right) hold constant screen positions across all frames, so the jet's trajectory does not translate.

The internal texture of the jet changes over time: in the early frames the column reads as a relatively smooth, bulging ribbon, while in the later frames the same column shows progressively more pronounced breakup into separate droplets and jagged tendrils, especially along its middle section.
The splash at the impact zone and the surrounding airborne droplets fluctuate in shape and position from frame to frame, indicating continuous spraying rather than a single frozen event.
The blurred grass and curb background remain fixed in position and framing, consistent with a stationary camera and no obvious pan or zoom.
The wet pavement patch and the bright reflection at the splash site persist across the whole segment without appearing or disappearing.
outside_clip_unknowns: The source or nozzle producing the liquid is outside the top edge of the frame, so how the stream is generated and whether it starts or stops within the full video is not shown.
The motion is already underway at the first frame and continues past the last; no onset or completion of the flow is captured.
What the liquid is, and any earlier cause of the stream, cannot be determined from these frames.
uncertain_details: The material identity of the liquid (e.g., water versus another pale fluid) is not determinable from appearance alone.
The increased droplet breakup in later frames could reflect the natural wave/instability phase of a continuous jet rather than a change in flow rate; the clip does not disambiguate this.
Camera motion is inferred as static from background stability, but sub-pixel drift cannot be confirmed.
Individual airborne droplets cannot be reliably tracked between frames, so their exact trajectories are not established.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
